video.title: 6 BORING Garage Businesses Anyone Can Start (Most Get Busier When It Gets Cold)

summary: A narrated listicle from Harry's Stealth Wealth presenting six garage-based businesses: furniture flipping, knife sharpening, bicycle repair/flipping, small engine repair, boat/RV shrink wrapping and ceramic coating/detailing. Each comes with cited price points, startup costs and example operators (e.g. Sarah Chen's dresser flips, Michael Kemp's $60k first-year knife sharpening, Go Detail's $75k/month). It frames a 'four-season bay' where services rotate with the weather and offers three filters to choose one. All are hands-on physical services with little automation potential.

ideas.name: Garage furniture flipping
ideas.one_liner: Buy solid-wood furniture cheap or from curbs, sand/prime/paint/new hardware, and resell on Facebook Marketplace.
ideas.business_model: Buy low, refinish, resell per piece
ideas.customer: Local buyers: people moving, first apartments, new homeowners
ideas.offer: Refinished solid-wood dressers, tables, nightstands, credenzas

pricing.notes: Rule: buy at half of retail or less; skip pieces that won't clear double the all-in cost.

acquisition_channels.details: Daylight driveway photos listed on Facebook Marketplace; relist weekend mornings.
Source via 20+ local buy-and-sell groups and curb finds.

ideas.delivery: Owner refinishes each piece (2-3 hours basic) in the garage.
unit_economics_claims: Nightstands net $40-110, dressers $100-250, dining sets $120-320, credenzas $200-450
ideas.startup_cost: $100-150; then $20-60 per piece for paint and hardware

acquisition.how: Listings can be drafted and posted by agents; sourcing needs a human eye.

uk_applicability.notes: Facebook Marketplace and furniture upcycling are popular in the UK.

risks: Pieces may not sell; seasonal slowdown in winter

quotes.text: A tall boy dresser sells for $325 to $425 and she buys it for $40 to 70
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: $35,000 in profit over 15 months. Her rule was simple. She buys at half of retail or less
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Knife sharpening with restaurant accounts
ideas.one_liner: Sharpen knives for $10-20 each with batching and recurring restaurant accounts, from a garage bench or car.
ideas.business_model: Per knife with pickup minimum; recurring restaurant accounts

acquisition_channels.details: Walk into restaurants at 3pm between lunch and dinner with a demo knife slicing paper.

quote.text: Walk in at 3:00 in the afternoon with one freshly sharpened knife and slice a sheet of paper in the air
quote.speaker: Narrator

ideas.delivery: Owner sharpens in batches (10-12 knives in ~90 minutes) on a belt grinder.

uk_applicability.notes: Restaurants exist in the UK; carrying knives in public has legal restrictions (good reason needed).

risks: Mixing up customers' knives (needs ticket system)

quotes.text: Michael Kemp in Austin, Texas, charges $10 to $20 a knife by size with a $150 pickup minimum
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: 10 or 12 knives take him about 90 minutes, barely longer than one
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Bicycle repair and refurb flipping
ideas.one_liner: Tune-ups and flipping used bikes, buying in winter and selling in spring; kids' bikes sell fast.
ideas.business_model: Per tune-up fees and bike resale margins
ideas.problem: Bike shops booked out in spring; kids outgrow bikes

acquisition_channels.details: Neighbours on Nextdoor asking who can fix a chain.

ideas.delivery: Owner repairs on a stand in the garage.
unit_economics_claims: Jeff: $60 bike sold for $200; ~$1k/year on a dozen bikes

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; strong cycling culture.

quotes.text: A Seattle hobbyist named Jeff puts $60 into an old touring bike and sold it for $200
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: Stan in Fremont, moves about 12 bikes a month at $100 to $850 each
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Small engine repair (mowers, snowblowers)
ideas.one_liner: Garage tune-ups and repairs of mowers and snowblowers, catching overflow from backlogged shops.
ideas.business_model: Labour per tune-up plus parts billed to customer
ideas.offer: Tune-ups and repairs; dead machines become parts or flips

pricing.notes: Parts billed through; labour is what you keep.

acquisition_channels.details: Hardware store counters and overflow from busy shops.

ideas.delivery: Owner repairs in the garage; learnt from free tutorials and manuals in 4-6 weeks.
ideas.startup_cost: $1-2k for used tools and parts shelf
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Month one a few hundred dollars

uk_applicability.notes: Mowers common in UK; snowblowers rare; check planning/home-occupation rules.

risks: Fuel storage fire risk and insurance

quotes.text: Tiger Small Engine Repair charges $75 plus parts for a push mower tuneup. 85 plus parts for a snowblower and 195 plus parts for a riding mower
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: They had roughly 500 machines waiting for service
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Boat and RV shrink wrapping
ideas.one_liner: Seasonal shrink-wrap winterisation for boats/RVs priced per foot, sourced via marinas and boat-owner groups.
ideas.business_model: Per foot pricing, seasonal; repeat each fall
ideas.offer: Shrink wrapping, often paired with winterisation

acquisition_channels.details: Local boat owner groups on Facebook.

ideas.delivery: Owner wraps on site with heat gun kit; checks support frame before quoting.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has boat owners but snow-driven demand is lower; marina markets differ.

risks: Pooled water from sagging frames causes callbacks

quotes.text: Shrink wrap is priced by the foot, usually about $8 to $25 a foot
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: 30 to 40 boats at $3 to $400 each is roughly $9 to $16,000 across an 8week window
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Garage detailing and ceramic coating
ideas.one_liner: Ceramic coatings and detailing from a dry garage bay; price by paint condition and hours.

pricing.notes: Price by paint condition and hours, not flat.

ideas.delivery: Owner details in garage after 4-6 weeks practice; optional coating certification.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Month 1 friends/family at discount; strangers by month 3

acquisition.how: GBP and photos can be partly automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Car detailing and ceramic coating popular in the UK.

ideas.one_liner: Combine seasonal services in one garage so the bay earns year-round.

tactics.name: Furniture flip buy rule
steps: Only buy solid wood
Total paint, hardware and hours before buying
Walk away unless sale clears double the all-in cost
Buy at half of retail or less
Join 20+ local buy-and-sell groups
Photograph in daylight on driveway; relist weekend mornings

tactics.name: Restaurant knife account demo
steps: Practise on own knives 2 weeks
Visit restaurants at ~3pm quiet hours
Slice paper in the air with a sharpened knife
Batch 10-12 knives per session
Set a pickup minimum

tactics.name: Drop-off ticket system
steps: Numbered ticket for every drop-off with name, phone, count and pickup date
Rule: no ticket, no tool touches it

quote.text: No ticket, no tool touches it
quote.speaker: Narrator

tactics.name: Boat wrap walkaround before quoting
steps: Measure the boat
Check support frame to avoid pooled water callbacks
Price per foot

tactics.name: Pick a garage business with three filters
steps: Fits your bay and power
Busy season starts within 60 days
First 3 customers reachable where buyers already look (Marketplace, Nextdoor, marina board)
Measure bay, count outlets, check 3 local shops' prices

tactics.name: Cross-sell seasonal services
steps: Wrap boat in October
Winterise mower and wake snowblower same visit

warnings.warning: Buying furniture first and counting costs later loses money.

quote.text: The thing beginners get wrong is buying first and counting later
quote.speaker: Narrator

warnings.warning: Store fuel outside the bay and drain tanks; insurance and fire code care.

quote.text: Store fuel outside the bay and drain every tank that comes in
quote.speaker: Narrator

warnings.warning: Check city home-occupation rules before running a garage business.
Mixed-up customer items cost time and trust; use tickets.
Pricing every detailing job the same is a mistake.

quote.text: The mistake new detailers make is pricing every car the same
quote.speaker: Narrator

warnings.warning: Propane safety and liability insurance are required for shrink wrapping.

lessons.lesson: A home garage is a business asset; you don't need a storefront.
Batching jobs dramatically increases hourly earnings.
Buy in the off season, sell in peak season (bikes: buy winter, sell spring).

quote.text: The Smart Rhythm is buying cheap in winter when nobody wants a bike and selling in spring when everybody does
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Overflow from backlogged established shops is a ready source of customers.
Stack seasonal services so the asset is used year-round.
Size the pond: you only need a tiny slice of local demand.
Price by condition and hours, not flat rates.
Learn your local market by checking what three shops charge.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand listicle citing press and price lists; Harry appears to be an illustrative character.
